Disclosed are methods and integrated circuit (IC) structures. The methods enable formation of a gate contact on a gate above (or close thereto) an active region of a field effect transistor (FET) and provide protection against shorts between the gate contact and metal plugs on source/drain regions and between the gate and source/drain contacts to the metal plugs. A gate with a dielectric cap and dielectric sidewall spacer is formed on a FET channel region. Metal plugs with additional dielectric caps are formed on the FET source/drain regions such that the dielectric sidewall spacer is between the gate and the metal plugs and between the dielectric cap and the additional dielectric caps. The dielectric cap, dielectric sidewall spacer and additional dielectric caps are different materials preselected to be selectively etchable, allowing for misalignment of a contact opening to the gate without risking exposure of any metal plugs and vice versa.

outputs.L1: Methods and integrated circuit (IC) structures are disclosed. The methods enable the formation of a gate contact on a gate above, or in close proximity to, an active region of a field-effect transistor (FET), while protecting against shorts between the gate contact and metal plugs on source/drain regions, as well as between gate and source/drain contacts to the metal plugs. A gate having a dielectric cap and a dielectric sidewall spacer is formed on a FET channel region. Metal plugs having additional dielectric caps are formed on the FET source/drain regions such that the dielectric sidewall spacer is positioned between the gate and the metal plugs and between the dielectric cap and the additional dielectric caps. The dielectric cap, dielectric sidewall spacer, and additional dielectric caps are formed from different materials preselected for selective etching, thereby allowing misalignment of a contact opening to the gate without risking exposure of any metal plugs, and vice versa.
outputs.L2: Methods and integrated-circuit (IC) configurations are described. These techniques permit a gate contact to be fabricated directly over, or near, an active region of a field-effect transistor (FET), while reducing the risk of electrical shorts between the gate contact and metal plugs associated with the source/drain regions, as well as between gate and source/drain contacts connected to those plugs. A gate structure having a dielectric cap and dielectric sidewall spacer is formed over the FET channel region. Metal plugs topped with additional dielectric caps are positioned on the source/drain regions so that the sidewall spacer separates the gate from the metal plugs and also lies between the gate’s dielectric cap and the additional caps. The gate cap, sidewall spacer, and plug caps are made from distinct materials selected for differential etchability. This arrangement accommodates misalignment of a gate-contact opening without exposing the metal plugs, and likewise permits misalignment in the opposite situation without exposing the gate.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed methods and integrated circuit (IC) structures enable a gate contact to be formed directly above or near an active region of a field-effect transistor (FET). This arrangement supports more compact device layouts while reducing the risk of unintended electrical connections.

To protect against short circuits, the design electrically isolates the gate contact from adjacent source/drain metal plugs and source/drain contacts. A gate structure is formed over the FET channel region and includes both a dielectric cap and a dielectric sidewall spacer. Metal plugs are formed over the source/drain regions and are likewise covered with additional dielectric caps. The gate sidewall spacer provides physical and electrical separation between the gate structure and the neighboring metal plugs, including their respective dielectric caps.

The dielectric caps and spacers are made from materials having different etch selectivities. As a result, contact openings can be patterned and etched with some degree of alignment tolerance. Even if a contact opening is misaligned, the selectively etchable dielectric components prevent the etch from exposing the gate or the source/drain metal plugs. This self-protecting configuration reduces the likelihood of shorts between the gate contact and the source/drain structures, thereby improving device reliability and enabling tighter feature spacing.
outputs.L4:
Methods of fabricating integrated-circuit structures are provided in which a gate contact can be formed near a field-effect transistor (FET) active region while reducing the risk of electrical shorts. A gate structure is formed over a semiconductor body and includes a conductive gate electrode covered by a dielectric gate cap and bordered by dielectric sidewall spacers. Source and drain regions are formed adjacent to the gate structure, and conductive metal plugs are formed to contact the source and drain regions. The source/drain metal plugs are separately covered by dielectric caps and may be made from a material that can be selectively etched relative to the surrounding dielectric materials and the gate conductor.

An interlayer dielectric is formed over the gate structure and the capped source/drain plugs. A contact opening for the gate is then patterned and etched through the interlayer dielectric. Because lithographic and etching processes may cause the contact opening to be displaced from its intended position, the opening may overlap a portion of a neighboring source/drain plug. The dielectric cap on the source/drain plug, together with the dielectric gate cap and sidewall spacers, protects the plug during formation of the gate-contact opening. Appropriate material selection and selective etch chemistries allow the opening to expose the conductive gate electrode without substantially removing the dielectric protection over the adjacent source/drain plug.

A conductive material is subsequently deposited in the gate-contact opening to form a gate contact. Even when the opening is misaligned toward a source or drain region, the protected source/drain plug remains electrically isolated from the gate contact. The resulting structure therefore permits reduced contact spacing and increased layout density while improving process tolerance and preventing unintended shorts between the gate contact and source/drain contacts.
outputs.L5:
### The FET Disclosed: A Key Component in Modern Electronics

The field-effect transistor, commonly known as the FET, is a fundamental component in modern electronic devices. Its primary function is to control the flow of electrical current through a semiconductor using an electric field. Because FETs consume little power and can switch signals rapidly, they are widely used in computers, smartphones, amplifiers, sensors, and power-management systems.

Recent technical reports have disclosed improvements in FET design, including smaller dimensions, better energy efficiency, and enhanced thermal performance. These developments could make future electronic systems faster and more reliable while reducing power consumption.

The FET exists in several forms, such as the MOSFET, JFET, and FinFET. Each type is designed for particular applications, from processing digital information to controlling high-power equipment. As semiconductor technology continues to advance, the FET will remain essential to the development of compact, efficient, and high-performance electronics.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention in which selectively etchable dielectric caps and sidewall spacers provide self-aligned gate and source/drain contacts despite contact-opening misalignment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, using formal patent language, how etch-selective dielectric materials can protect gate contacts and source/drain contacts from accidental exposure and electrical shorts during IC fabrication.
counterfactuals.output:
In certain embodiments, an integrated circuit structure comprises a gate electrode disposed over a semiconductor body, a source/drain region positioned adjacent to the gate electrode, and respective conductive contacts coupled to the gate electrode and the source/drain region. One or more dielectric protection structures are arranged between, over, and/or along sidewalls of the conductive contacts. The dielectric protection structures comprise materials having different etch characteristics with respect to a selected etchant.

For example, a gate contact may be covered or laterally bounded by a first dielectric material, while a source/drain contact is covered or laterally bounded by a second dielectric material. The first dielectric material is selected to exhibit a substantially lower etch rate than the second dielectric material during formation of a source/drain contact opening. Accordingly, an etch process used to remove the second dielectric material preferentially removes material over the source/drain region while substantially preserving the first dielectric material over or adjacent to the gate contact.

If a lithographically defined source/drain contact opening is laterally misaligned and extends partially over the gate contact, the preserved first dielectric material functions as an etch-stop or protective barrier. The barrier prevents, or at least reduces, exposure of the gate contact to the contact-opening etch and to subsequently deposited conductive material. Thus, conductive material filling the source/drain contact opening is inhibited from physically contacting the gate contact, thereby reducing the likelihood of an electrical short between the gate electrode and the source/drain region.

Conversely, the second dielectric material may be resistant to an etchant used to form a gate-contact opening. In such an arrangement, an overextended or misaligned gate-contact opening does not substantially remove dielectric material protecting the source/drain contact. The source/drain contact consequently remains electrically isolated from conductive material deposited in the gate-contact opening.

Suitable etch-selective material combinations may include, by way of non-limiting example, silicon oxide, silicon nitride, silicon carbide, silicon carbon nitride, silicon oxycarbide, silicon oxynitride, aluminum oxide, hafnium oxide, or combinations thereof. The materials and etch chemistry may be selected such that an etch-rate ratio between a material intended to be removed and a material intended to remain is sufficiently high to preserve a desired protective thickness throughout the contact-opening process.

In some embodiments, the etch-selective dielectric material forms a cap over a conductive feature, a spacer along a sidewall of the conductive feature, a liner surrounding the conductive feature, or a combination thereof. Such structures provide a self-aligned contact scheme in which the ultimate contact boundary is determined at least partially by the etch-resistant dielectric structures rather than solely by lithographic alignment.

Accordingly, etch selectivity provides process tolerance for overlay error, critical-dimension variation, and etch overrun. By maintaining dielectric separation between neighboring conductive features notwithstanding partial overlap of a patterned opening, the disclosed arrangement protects gate contacts and source/drain contacts from accidental exposure and suppresses formation of conductive bridges and gate-to-source/drain electrical shorts.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent covering methods and integrated-circuit structures that enable contact-over-active-gate formation with misalignment tolerance through differentiated dielectric caps and spacers.
counterfactuals.output: Methods and integrated-circuit structures are provided for forming a contact over an active gate region with increased misalignment tolerance. A gate structure is formed over a semiconductor active region and includes a gate electrode, a dielectric gate cap, and dielectric sidewall spacers. The gate cap and at least one portion of the sidewall spacers comprise dielectric materials having different etch characteristics relative to one or more surrounding interlayer dielectrics. A contact opening is patterned over the active gate region and may be laterally misaligned with an underlying source/drain contact region. During etching, the differentiated gate cap and spacers protect the gate electrode while permitting the contact opening to extend along a side of the gate structure to expose the contact region. The contact opening is filled with conductive material to form a contact electrically coupled to the contact region and electrically isolated from the gate electrode. Material selectivity and cap-and-spacer geometry thereby provide self-alignment and enhanced process-margin control.
